Ramp-up = capacity ceiling (cap), not a forecast flight count (ASTRA_AUDIT B1/P3). 2027/28 = company plan (4 flights 2027, doubling 2028, https://payloadspace.com/seops-books-five-launches-on-isars-spectrum-rocket/), 2029/30 team assumption, 2031–2035 team assumption (D-027): extrapolation up to factory capacity of 40/year (https://europeanspaceflight.com/isar-aerospace-announces-new-launch-date-alongside-series-d-funding/) as the ceiling; no entry from 2036, because the corridor has no E3 point values. In the 2030 base run the cap does not bind (Astra: 10.76 missions at cap 18). 2026 added (D-017): flight 2 reached orbit on 05.09.2026, at most one further launch in the rest of 2026 (team assumption). Plan v2 section 5. Factory target 'up to 40 rockets/year' is production capacity, not cadence. Manifest plausibility: 2028 'at least four flights' and 2028 manifest full (https://payloadspace.com/seops-books-five-launches-on-isars-spectrum-rocket/); SEOPS 5 dedicated launches 2028–2030 from Andøya and Nova Scotia (same source); Astroscale ADRAS-J2 2027/28 (https://isaraerospace.com/press/isar-aerospace-signs-launch-contract-with-astroscale-japan) and ELSA-M FY2028+ (https://isaraerospace.com/press/isar-aerospace-secures-first-active-debris-removal-mission-with-astroscale); NO AOS, ESA missions. rows.source: Team assumption (Isar does not publish a price list)
rows.note: Derivation: price target ~10 k€/kg × 700 kg SSO = €7 million as lower bound; benchmark Electron ~US$8.4 million ASP on new contracts Q3 2024 (https://www.fool.com/investing/2024/11/18/rocket-lab-is-raising-prices-and-happy-about-it), Spectrum has ~2–3× Electron payload. Plan: €9 million.
Each kg above 50 kg. History: 2019 5,000 $/kg, 2024 6,500 $/kg (https://payloadspace.com/spacex-increases-rideshare-prices). Rideshare page is JS-rendered; value confirmed via secondary source.
ECB reference rate 15.09.2026: 1 EUR = 1.1539 USD -> 0.867 EUR/USD (plan default 0.85).

Plan v2 section 5; missing cells = 0. EU_ESA×D 0.60: sovereignty/defense customers (Bundeswehr, NO AOS) prefer European access; rideshare often ruled out. EU_ESA×C 0.50: ESA/EU preference for European launchers (ESA Boost!, ELC), but Vega-C/Ariane 6 and competitors RFA/PLD. EU_ESA×C/D 0.50/0.60 = uncalibrated team assumption; European preference does not mean an automatic contract award; ownership control and launch site (Canada) to be checked separately. The earlier claim “ESA definition excludes Isar” has been removed (ASTRA_AUDIT.md B2): on 05.07.2024 ESA explicitly named Isar as a European provider; ELC contract 27.08.2026 (https://www.esa.int/Enabling_Support/Space_Transportation/First_contracts_kick_off_European_Launcher_Challenge). Sensitivity via ±20% tornado (sensitivity.pct), no separate switch. EU_ESA×B 0.30: commercial, price-sensitive, SpaceX rideshare 7,000 $/kg vs. ~13 k€/kg Spectrum; only customers who need their own orbit/schedule. EU_ESA×A 0.25: university/education CubeSats, ESA Fly Your Satellite, price-sensitive. ALLIED×B 0.10 / ×C 0.15: partner states (JP, CA, KR, AU) have their own/US options; Isar has no home advantage. US×B 0.05: US market difficult (Rocket Lab, Firefly, SpaceX, Buy American). US×C, ×D, ALLIED×A/D = 0.

D-021, optional: win rate per (state_group, class, vertical) as {state_group: {class: {vertical: rate}}}. An entry overrides the winrate_matrix cell for that vertical only; empty = existing matrix (default).
